User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user in the GoalForge application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

coins.description: The number of coins the user has.

streak.description: The user's current streak of consecutive challenge completions.

goalId.description: Reference to the user's current Goal. (Relationship: User 1:1 Goal)

friendIds.description: References to the user's friends (other User ids). (Relationship: User N:N User)

id.description: Unique identifier for the goal entity.

description.description: A description of the goal (e.g., 'Lose 5kg', 'Learn Python').

startDate.description: The date and time when the goal was started.

userId.description: Reference to the user who set this goal. (Relationship: User 1:1 Goal)

ChallengeTemplate.title: ChallengeTemplate
ChallengeTemplate.description: Represents a template for a challenge, categorized by goal type.

id.description: Unique identifier for the challenge template.

goalType.description: The type of goal this challenge is associated with (e.g., 'Weight Loss', 'Coding').

description.description: The text description of the challenge (e.g., 'Drink 3L water', 'Solve 1 LeetCode problem').

UserChallenge.title: UserChallenge
UserChallenge.description: Represents a specific challenge assigned to a user for a particular day.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user challenge.

userId.description: Reference to the user who is assigned this challenge. (Relationship: User 1:N UserChallenge)

challengeTemplateId.description: Reference to the challenge template used to create this challenge. (Relationship: ChallengeTemplate 1:N UserChallenge)

assignedDate.description: The date when this challenge was assigned to the user.

completed.description: Indicates whether the user has completed the challenge.

completionTimestamp.description: The timestamp when the challenge was completed, or null if not completed.

FriendRequest.title: FriendRequest
FriendRequest.description: Represents a friend request from one user to another.

id.description: Unique identifier for the friend request.

senderId.description: The UID of the user sending the request.

senderName.description: The name of the user sending the request.

senderEmail.description: The email of the user sending the request.

receiverId.description: The UID of the user receiving the request.

definition.description: Stores user profiles.  Authentication is enforced at this level.  Only the user can read/write their own profile.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user, corresponding to their Firebase Auth UID.

definition.description: Stores goals associated with a specific user. This enforces the relationship User 1:1 Goal. Only the owning user can access these goal.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user, corresponding to their Firebase Auth UID.

params.name: goalId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user's goal.

definition.description: Stores challenge templates. Accessible by all users to fetch and populate challenges.

params.name: challengeTemplateId
params.description: The unique identifier for the challenge template.

definition.description: Stores user challenges assigned to a specific user. Enforces path-based ownership, restricting access to only the owning user.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user, corresponding to their Firebase Auth UID.

params.name: userChallengeId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user challenge.

definition.description: Stores friend requests sent to a user in a subcollection. Security rules enforce that users can only manage requests sent to them.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user receiving the request.

params.name: requestId
params.description: The unique identifier for the friend request.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure has been updated to use a subcollection model for friend requests (/users/{userId}/friendRequests). This is a more secure and scalable approach than a root-level 'friendRequests' collection. It simplifies security rules by tying data directly to the user who owns it, ensuring users can only query and manage their own incoming requests. This change resolves persistent permission errors related to listing friend requests.
